Table from [8]. 13.2 Impacts of State, Local, and Tribal Regulations on MTV At this project stage, there is insufficient information to formulate the requirements of specific state, local, or tribal regulations because all sites have not been identified. While additional authorizations may be required locally, federal processes will likely constitute the majority of regulatory requirements. Because the MTV will only be used over submerged lands, many local requirements for grid-connected projects will not apply. Therefore at minimum, consultation is expected to be required by state, local, and tribal regulations. Most data collection and analysis will likely be provided during federal authorization. 13.3 PROPOSED MTV REGULATORY STRATEGY Commissioning the MTV will involve a DOE NEPA review. Additional regulatory compliance may be required once CEC developers request the use of the MTV. Therefore, the overall MTV regulatory strategy was to address each situation separately but leverage any documentation, processes, consultations, and authorizations resulting from the project’s NEPA review to inform in-service regulatory needs. 13.3.1 Commissioning Regulatory Strategy At the current project stage (Final Design), sufficiently detailed information is available for a NEPA review of the MTV for commissioning, but a final selection was not made for commissioning site(s) and commissioning CEC(s). The goal of MTV site and CEC selection for commissioning will be to facilitate the ability to apply a DOE Categorical Exclusion (CX) to avoid requiring a detailed environmental review and incurring potentially significant project delay. A conceptual DOE NEPA review process is illustrated in Figure 13-2. Final Technical Report 43/57 Figure 13-2: Conceptual DOE NEPA process Securing DOE NEPA approval to commission the MTV will also be useful in informing an in-service regulatory approach by identifying primary regulatory considerations with respect to the MTV and performing agency consultations. Resulting data, analyses, and determinations will be leveraged to provide a baseline that may be transferrable to other sites and for other CEC technologies but, at minimum, will inform MTV platform-specific regulatory risks and mitigation options. 13.3.2 In-service Regulatory Strategy It is not expected that full authorization for MTV lifetime use can be achieved in advance, given the dependence of regulatory approvals on specific site conditions and CEC characteristics. Therefore, the MTV in-service regulatory strategy aims to address as many requirements as possible in advance of use to lower barriers to permitting by amassing data and documentation to expedite future approvals.
